visualReview.notes: Inspected seven current portable views. The whitewashed street corner, red tiled gable, two stepped doors, five front openings, and tall side openings are distinct. The elevated views show a clear gap between the two roofed bodies and the open gate.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected seven current shared-material views, including the bounded dated placement. Whitewashed walls, warm ribbed tile, brick stair treads, timber and dark iron remain distinct. The north-up frame shows the envelope and open court aligned with the mapped street corner.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 23 context, detail, and transition frames. Both gabled roofs, the garden court, and the gateway opening persist at every authored level. Closer levels refine the arched heads, grille bars, and clay tile rolls.

geographicReview.notes: The envelope follows the native five-corner ring of OpenStreetMap way 390842545. The named museum node and separately mapped alley establish the site. In the original unmasked field view, the stepped façade and foundation meet the original coarse street terrain. Threshold and vertical registration are approximate.

fidelityReview.scope: The street-corner Casa de la Independencia Museum in Asunción as seen in the two early published color references. Includes the whitewashed street wings, clay-tile roofs, raised entrance steps, open central garden court, and the gateway on 14 de Mayo. Omits interior exhibits, the separately mapped historic alley and the later recovery of the adjacent former stable lot.
fidelityReview.notes: Exact published exterior images support the street corner and 14 de Mayo gateway. The municipal inventory establishes two roofed bodies around an open garden. Roof pitch, courtyard boundaries, unseen rear wing and gallery and local grade are modeled estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Inspected two published Qualla originals from Mil va and Fernando Boccia. Both match exact Commons SHA-1, pinned revisions and explicit creator public-domain dedications. The corner image has no independently established capture date. Only the depicted exterior informed the model.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: restored corner house, two roof masses, open courtyard and 14 de Mayo gateway in an early exterior view

limitations: The corner façade and 14 de Mayo gateway follow exact published public-domain Qualla originals. The corner view was published in 2008 and lacks an independently established exposure date.
The older restoration is shown in early color photographs. The later recovery of the former stable property, alley paving, adjacent buildings and museum interior are outside the scope.

The mapped outline establishes the exterior extents. Internal court edges, the unphotographed rear wing and gallery, roof rise, facade dimensions, and plinth and step grades are proportioned estimates.
The 128 m original elevation field was sampled before floors and sections were chosen. No terrain leveling, masking or reference photo pixels are included.
